I was listening to Fox News in the background this morning. They were talking about how Putin navigated the collapse of the Soviet Union and how he's now navigating the collapse of the European Union. They accused him of helping cause it by barrel bombing Syria and escalating the migrant crisis. They said Russia could end up cutting off natural gas to Europe and causing a bigger crisis.

Then I heard a talking head reference Kissinger's talks with Putin, and how Kissinger warned that we should "expect Russia to do things we least want them to do."

I had to find a source for such a statement.

I googled this phrase and others like it and didn't come up with anything. I also specified a timeline after the Feb 3 2016 meeting the talking head was referencing. I did find a Newsweek article that accuses Kissinger of not having a clue how to fix current gaps in US-Russian relations. That's about it.

I also noticed a lot of other sources referencing constant phone conversations between Putin and Kissinger in early 2016. These sources were all either Russo-centric media outlets (sputniknews, kremlin.ru, RT, pravdareport) or alt-right digests (infowars, trunews, fort-russ the alt-RT outlet), along with a youtube video predictably claiming that they were discussing the NWO.

It's not the content of these sources that interested me, it was the notable lack of mainstream coverage. Just googling "putin kissinger" after Feb 3 brings up that Newsweek thing and the NY Post. No big outlets on Pages 2, 3, 4, etc.

Now, I know google has been accused of censorship and result steering. I'm furious about that. Yet, here google is, giving me content from sites that likely do not align with their paradigm, on a topic that the mainstream media apparently refused to cover.

So, I binged "putin kissinger" and limited the results to post-Feb 3 again. Not much else. No NYT. No WaPo. No Tribune, Times, etc. Politico did a story on Feb 4 about how GOP primary candidates were lining up to kiss Kissinger's proverbial statesmanship ring, and mentioned Kissinger's latest book, suspiciously titled "World Order" (jeez Henry, you're going to set the conspiracy world on fire).

I'm not one for paranoia. Maybe the meeting just wasn't that newsworthy. Maybe the liberal media are so angry at Kissinger's "war crimes" that they refuse to give him the press. Who knows, all I know is that the end-of-week of Feb 3-6 saw two viral news stories: Zika (no pun intended) and the Manhattan crane collapse.

It seems to me that if Politico would run a front page story on primary candidates scrambling to meet with Kissinger, some reputable newspaper would run a small backpage piece on his meeting with the leader of another superpower. Even Foreign Policy magazine (foreignpolicy.com) didn't run a Putin-Kissinger story the entire month of February. wtf
